criteria.text: `gates-conformance` CI job blocks correctly on all seven seeded fixtures independently: coverage regression, flaky-then-passing test, planted secret, vulnerable dependency, SAST finding, disabled-check diff, missing green `engine-live` record.

citations.ref: gates-conformance / gates-conformance (ubuntu-latest), job 91480518492, step "seeded-fault matrix (7 independent fixtures) blocks correctly"
citations.quotedAssertion: job log line 195 — 'npx vitest run packages/gates/src/gates-conformance.test.ts --coverage.enabled=false'; line 201 — '✓  @crabgic/gates  src/gates-conformance.test.ts (7 tests) 48ms'; lines 203-204 — ' Test Files  1 passed (1)' / '      Tests  7 passed (7)'. This is the job the criterion names, at this record's own base commit, and the step log shows it really executed this suite rather than merely being green.

.github/workflows/gates-conformance.yml:18-21 — 'on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:'; :27-28 'jobs:
  gates-conformance:'; :43-44 '- name: seeded-fault matrix (7 independent fixtures) blocks correctly
        run: npx vitest run packages/gates/src/gates-conformance.test.ts --coverage.enabled=false'. The job name the criterion cites exists, is standalone-runnable, and fires on every push and PR — not a manual-dispatch-only workflow like engine-live/jira-datacenter-smoke.

One `it()` per named fixture, each asserting the BLOCK rather than the pass: :57 '1. coverage regression: a recorded floor of 82% followed by a 79% run BLOCKS' / :79 'expect(result?.verdict.passed).toBe(false);'; :82 '2. flaky-then-passing test' / :94-95 'expect(result?.verdict.unstable).toBe(true); expect(result?.verdict.passed).toBe(false);'; :98 '3. planted secret' (a 20-char `AKIA`-prefixed fixture key at :115, not reproduced here — this repository's own pre-commit secret scanner rejects the literal even inside prose) / :121; :127 '4. vulnerable dependency' (`CVE-2024-22222`, CRITICAL, at :147) / :157; :163 '5. SAST finding' (`javascript.lang.security.audit.sqli`, severity ERROR, at :178-180) / :187; :193 '6. disabled-check diff' ('+  // assert(result === expected);' at :198) / :201; :204 '7. missing green engine-live record' / :212. Seven fixtures, seven independent assertions, in the order the criterion lists them.

packages/gates/src/gates-conformance.test.ts:35-42 — 'beforeEach(async () => { tj = await createTestJournal(); baseContext = { changeSetId: randomUUID(), journal: tj.store }; }); afterEach(async () => { await tj.cleanup(); });'. This is the 'independently' clause: every fixture gets a fresh on-disk journal, and each `it()` builds its own `createGateRegistry()` (:58, :69, :83, :103, :132, :169, :194, :205), with fixtures 3-5 additionally each mkdtemp'ing their own `CapabilityStore` root (:99, :128, :164). No fixture's pass or failure can mask another's.

The anti-vacuity control for fixtures 3-5. :289 'a clean run across every registered scanner passes overall' registers semgrep, gitleaks and osv-scanner against clean reports and :323 asserts 'expect(results.every((r) => r.verdict.passed)).toBe(true);'. Without it, three gates that always returned `passed: false` would satisfy the criterion's three security fixtures.

The anti-vacuity control for fixture 6. :156 'root-cause detector stays advisory (non-blocking) by default' fires the SAME diff text the blocking fixture uses ('+  // assert(result === expected);', :161) with no `blocking: true`, and :168 asserts 'expect(result?.verdict.passed).toBe(true);'. So fixture 6's block is caused by the configured policy, not by the detector refusing everything.

The anti-vacuity control for fixture 1. :23 'passes a greenfield project at/above the 80% minimum on both axes' / :38 'expect(result?.verdict.passed).toBe(true);'. Paired with :118-149, where the 82% run is asserted to pass first (:133) before the 79% run blocks (:149), so the block is the regression's doing.

The anti-vacuity control for fixture 2. :22 'a clean first-attempt pass is green and NOT unstable' / :34-35 'expect(result?.verdict.passed).toBe(true); expect(result?.verdict.unstable).toBeUndefined();'. The `unstable` flag is therefore a discriminating signal, not a constant.

The anti-vacuity control for fixture 7. :74 'a matching green engine-live record's run ID round-trips into the ChangeSet's EvidenceRecord' / :94 'expect(result?.verdict.passed).toBe(true);'. The engine-conformance gate can pass, so fixture 7's fail-closed is caused by the absent record.

'Test Files  2 passed (2)' / '      Tests  11 passed (11)' — supplementary scoped local re-run of the two suites this workflow runs, at `eabb65a`, with each of the seven fixture names printed individually by `--reporter=verbose`. Header records the UTC timestamp, HEAD sha, verbatim command and exit status 0.

criteria.notes: Scope, stated plainly because the criterion's word 'blocks' invites an overread. Every one of the seven fixtures is a PARSER/POLICY fixture, not a tool invocation: no semgrep, gitleaks or osv-scanner binary is executed anywhere in this phase (`docs/evidence/phase-14/README.md` §'What is fixture-modeled vs live'). What the seven assertions prove is that a seeded finding of each named shape produces a blocking `GateVerdict` — which is what a gate registry can be responsible for — not that the real scanners detect these things. The digest-pin half IS real: fixtures 3-5 resolve against an actual temp-directory-backed `@crabgic/detect` `CapabilityStore` (`createCapabilityStore`, :101/:130/:167), and `security-gate.test.ts:247-284` proves resolution fails closed on a digest mismatch and on a missing pinned entry. Later phases (21, 24) added gates to `packages/gates` without extending this matrix; the criterion enumerates exactly seven fixtures and makes no exhaustiveness claim over the registry's whole gate set, so that is not drift.

criteria.text: Coverage ratchet floor is monotonic non-decreasing across a simulated multi-`ChangeSet` history (fast-check property report, CI-archived).

citations.quotedAssertion: packages/gates/src/coverage/ratchet.property.test.ts:82 — '      { numRuns: 30 },' closes the fast-check assertion whose body asserts the floor never decreases across a monotonically-applied random sequence, checked incrementally after every observation on a real on-disk journal. The order-independence property above it is its anti-vacuity partner: a floor implementation that ignored history entirely would satisfy monotonicity and fail order-independence.

citations.ref: gates-conformance / gates-conformance (ubuntu-latest), step "coverage-ratchet monotonicity property report"
citations.quotedAssertion: job log line 266 — ' ✓  @crabgic/gates  src/coverage/ratchet.property.test.ts > coverage ratchet — property: final floor is order-independent (componentwise max of the whole history) > the floor never decreases across a monotonically-applied random sequence (also checked incrementally) 352ms' (one-space rule). The multi-ChangeSet history the criterion names is the randomized observation sequence each fast-check run builds.

The 'CI-archived' conjunct, which had no bearer at all before this change: `gh api repos/WitchyNibbles/crabgic/actions/runs/31087616366/artifacts` reports 'ratchet-property-report-ubuntu-latest  964 bytes' and 'ratchet-property-report-ubuntu-24.04-arm  966 bytes'. Per-arch names because two matrix legs sharing one artifact name would fail the second upload; `if-no-files-found: error` so an empty upload cannot satisfy it.

criteria.notes: Split criterion, and only the second half was ever in doubt. The property itself was already evidenced and non-vacuous, running inside the default npm test fan-out on every push. 'CI-archived' was simply untrue: no workflow uploaded a report. gates-conformance.yml now produces and uploads one per matrix leg. What the artifact contains is stated in the workflow rather than oversold — a per-property pass line with duration, a header pinning run/commit/runner, and on failure fast-check's counterexample and seed. An earlier draft set a CRABGIC_FASTCHECK_VERBOSE env var and claimed the report would record per-case counts; nothing reads that variable and fast-check does not print those on success, so it was removed rather than left as an inert control with a comment vouching for it.

criteria.text: `Requirement → EvidenceRecord → exact object ID` resolves in both directions for a fixture `ChangeSet` (named integration test).

packages/gates/src/requirement-resolution.test.ts:65-66 — 'expect(evidence!.objectId).toBe("exact-object-under-test"); expect(evidence!.requirementId).toBe(requirement.id);'. This is the EvidenceRecord→Requirement and EvidenceRecord→objectId half: the record fired for this `Requirement` carries both identities, so an object ID resolves back to the requirement that demanded it.

packages/gates/src/evidence.ts:76-80 — 'for await (const entry of journal.queryEntries({ type: "evidence_pointer" })) { if (entry.type !== "evidence_pointer") continue; if (entry.payload.requirementId === requirementId) { results.push(entry.payload); } }'. The reverse resolution is a real journal scan on a real field, not a lookup table the test populated; `requirementId` reaches the record from `GateContext` at :33 and is written by the single `emitEvidence` path.

'Test Files  8 passed (8)' / '      Tests  38 passed (38)' — supplementary scoped local re-run at `eabb65a`, including '✓ |@crabgic/gates| src/requirement-resolution.test.ts > Requirement -> EvidenceRecord -> exact object ID resolves in both directions > resolves forward (Requirement.evidenceRecordIds -> EvidenceRecord.objectId) and in reverse (requirementId -> journal -> EvidenceRecord -> objectId)'.

criteria.notes: One assertion in this test is VACUOUS and is deliberately NOT cited above, recorded here rather than silently dropped. :63-64 builds `const requirementWithEvidence = { ...requirement, evidenceRecordIds: [evidence!.id] };` and then asserts `expect(requirementWithEvidence.evidenceRecordIds).toContain(evidence!.id);` — a tautology over a literal the line above just wrote. It cannot fail, and it evidences nothing. The test's own comment is honest about why ("as 11 would, once it assembles the bidirectional mapping"): NOTHING in `packages/gates` populates `Requirement.evidenceRecordIds`. Grepping the whole tree, the only writers of that field are `packages/supervisor/src/intake/contract-builder.ts:84` (11's own intake) and `packages/learning/src/proposal-store/registry.ts:159` for the separate `LearningProposal` shape. That is consistent with this phase's declared boundary — roadmap/14 §Out of scope, "`IntentContract`/`Requirement` authoring and section structure (11)" — so the criterion is met by the two REAL directions the cited assertions carry (requirementId→journal→EvidenceRecord→objectId, and EvidenceRecord→requirementId), not by the field-population half the vacuous line gestures at. A reader who assumed the `evidenceRecordIds` round-trip was under test here would be wrong, which is why it is written down.

The quarantine entries are journaled as `adjudication_decision` — see criterion 7's note for why that is correct and not a contradiction of this phase's `evidence_pointer` posture.

criteria.text: TDD gate rejects a fixture attempt lacking a red-before-green `EvidenceRecord` pair for the same `Requirement`.

citations.ref: CI / unit-test+coverage (ubuntu-latest), job 91480519773, step "test with 80% line+branch coverage gate"
citations.quotedAssertion: job log line 541 — '✓  @crabgic/gates  src/tdd-gate.test.ts (10 tests) 66ms'

packages/gates/src/tdd-gate.test.ts:23 'fails closed when no red baseline has ever been captured for the requirement' / :47-48 'expect(result?.verdict.passed).toBe(false); expect(result?.verdict.detail).toMatch(/no red-baseline/i);' — note the gate is handed 'exitStatus: 0' (:34), i.e. a GREEN candidate, so the rejection is caused by the missing red half and not by a failing test run.

The 'for the same `Requirement`' clause: :314 'a red baseline for a DIFFERENT requirement does not satisfy this requirement's TDD gate' — a genuine `captureRedBaseline` is journaled for `otherRequirementId` (:318-325), the candidate is green (:334), and :347 asserts 'expect(result?.verdict.passed).toBe(false);'. Without this, requirement-scoping would be untested and any red baseline anywhere would pass the gate.

The 'red-BEFORE-green' clause, and the subtlest bearer in the file: :215 'the gate's OWN prior failing verdict must NOT retroactively satisfy its own red-baseline precondition on a later firing, when both firings share the same dispatch-boundary cutoff'. Firing #1 runs with no `captureRedBaseline` call anywhere in the test and journals its own tdd-tagged, nonzero-exit EvidenceRecord at seq 1; firing #2 reports green ('exitStatus: 0,' at :264) and :270 asserts 'expect(secondResult?.verdict.passed).toBe(false);'. The ordering belt is `beforeSeq` — :229 'const DISPATCH_BOUNDARY = 1;' — and :183-213 proves the cutoff is strict: :211 'expect(await hasRedBaseline(tj.store, requirementId, beforeSeq)).toBe(false);' against :212 'expect(await hasRedBaseline(tj.store, requirementId, (beforeSeq ?? 0) + 100)).toBe(true);'.

The anti-vacuity control: :51 'passes once a red baseline was journaled first and the candidate run is green' / :84-85 'expect(result?.verdict.passed).toBe(true); expect(result?.verdict.detail).toMatch(/red-baseline confirmed/i);'. Reinforced by :273-312, which passes only because the red baseline sits strictly before the supplied boundary ('beforeSeq: (redSeq ?? 0) + 1', :300). The gate is therefore capable of passing, so its rejections carry information.

The two remaining edges of the 'pair': :88-122 reports the candidate as still failing when a red baseline exists but the candidate has not gone green — :120-121 'expect(result?.verdict.passed).toBe(false);' / 'expect(result?.verdict.detail).toMatch(/still failing/i);' — so a green candidate is genuinely required, not just a red predecessor; and :124-135 'captureRedBaseline refuses a "red" baseline that already passes (exitStatus 0)', :134 ').rejects.toThrow(RedBaselineNotFailingError);' — the red half cannot be forged by journaling a passing run and calling it a baseline.
'Test Files  8 passed (8)' / '      Tests  38 passed (38)' — supplementary scoped local re-run at `eabb65a`; the verbose output names all ten tdd-gate cases individually.

criteria.notes: `docs/evidence/phase-14/README.md`'s row for this box says '8 tests'; the file at HEAD has 10 (two were added later — the `gateVerdict` shape test at :148-159 and one more from the adversarial round). The README's list is otherwise accurate. Quoted the tests, not the README, per the pass rule.

criteria.text: A stub external gate registers into the registry and fires at `final_verifying` with zero code change inside `packages/gates` (registry-extensibility conformance test).

citations.quotedAssertion: job log line 556 — '✓  @crabgic/gates  src/registry.test.ts (8 tests) 58ms'; line 577 — '✓  @crabgic/gates  src/registry.property.test.ts (1 test) 275ms'

packages/gates/src/registry.test.ts:115 'external extensibility — work item 6 / registry-extensibility conformance test'; :122-126 'function registerExternalGate(target: GateRegistry): void {' / 'target.register("performance", "15-external-perf-gate", async () =>' / 'stubVerdict(true, "external gate ran"),'; fired with :131 'stage: "final_verifying",' and asserted at :135-137 'expect(results).toHaveLength(1);' / 'expect(results[0]?.name).toBe("15-external-perf-gate");' / 'expect(results[0]?.evidence.gateTag).toBe("performance");'. The `performance` tag is 15's, which nothing in this package registers under, so the firing cannot be another gate's.

packages/gates/src/registry.test.ts:140-141 — 'const allResults = await registry.fireAll({ ...context, objectId: "integrated-obj-2" }); expect(allResults.some((r) => r.name === "15-external-perf-gate")).toBe(true);'. The external gate is reachable through the final-candidate re-verification path (`fireAll`), not only through the tag it was registered under — which is what makes criterion 8's 'full registered gate set' claim include external registrants.

The mechanism the test exercises is the same one this package's own gates use: :60-63 'register(tag, name, handler) {' / 'const existing = byTag.get(tag) ?? [];' / 'byTag.set(tag, [...existing, { tag, name, handler }]);' and :53-56 'async function fireOne(gate: RegisteredGate, context: GateContext): Promise<GateFireResult> {' / 'const verdict = await gate.handler(context);' / 'const evidence = await emitEvidence(context.journal, context, gate.tag, verdict);'. There is no allowlist of registrant identities and no branch on `gate.name` anywhere in the file — a registrant is a `(tag, name, handler)` triple and nothing else.

Real-world corroboration, not a stub: phase 24's acceptance-criteria seal gate is registered through this exact public API — :43 'export function registerCriteriaSealGate(' and :47 'registry.register("acceptance", "criteria-seal", async (context): Promise<GateVerdict> => {' — under the EXISTING `acceptance` tag (:24-26 'Registered under the EXISTING `acceptance` risk tag — one of the 13' / '`GATE_RISK_TAGS`, itself derived from the IntentContract's own section' / 'keys. No new tag'). `git show --stat 663dd08 -- packages/gates/src/registry.ts packages/gates/src/risk-tags.ts packages/gates/src/types.ts` is EMPTY: that PR added 195 lines across `criteria-seal-gate.ts`, its test, four barrel lines in `index.ts` and two lines in `final-candidate.e2e.test.ts`, and changed nothing in the registry, the tag vocabulary or the handler type. A later phase really did register a new gate with zero change to the registry.

'Test Files  8 passed (8)' / '      Tests  38 passed (38)' — supplementary scoped local re-run at `eabb65a`, whose verbose output names 'external extensibility — work item 6 / registry-extensibility conformance test > a stub EXTERNAL gate registers and fires at final_verifying with zero code change inside this package's own modules'.

criteria.notes: Two boundaries a reader should not have to infer. (a) 'External' is SIMULATED — `registerExternalGate` is defined inside `registry.test.ts`, in `packages/gates` itself, and no package outside `packages/gates` imports `createGateRegistry` at HEAD (grepped across `packages/*/src` and `e2e/*/src`). What the test proves is that the public API suffices; the phase-24 citation above is the closest thing to a real out-of-phase registrant, and it lives in the same package. 15's performance gate and 21's connector-security fixtures are named in the roadmap as the intended external registrants; 21's material actually landed INSIDE `packages/gates` (`materiality-*.ts`, `remote-verification-*.ts`, `traceability-view.ts`, `security-fixture-manifest.ts`, all added in `74bed14`), so the cross-package half of the aggregation pattern has never been exercised by a real caller. (b) The 'zero code change' guarantee holds for a gate registered under one of the 13 EXISTING tags. A registrant wanting a NEW tag would need `risk-tags.ts` edited, because `GATE_RISK_TAGS` is `as const` and `register`'s `tag` parameter is typed `GateRiskTag` — the criterion claims only the former, and phase 24 is the worked example of it.

criteria.text: Every emitted `EvidenceRecord` round-trips as a `JournalEntryType.evidence_pointer` entry through 02's discriminated-union exhaustiveness check.

citations.ref: CI / unit-test+coverage (ubuntu-latest), job 91480519773, step "test with 80% line+branch coverage gate"
citations.quotedAssertion: job log line 572 — '✓  @crabgic/gates  src/conformance.test.ts (3 tests) 40ms'; line 562 — '✓  @crabgic/gates  src/evidence.test.ts (5 tests) 52ms'

The round-trip itself: :61 'fires a gate, then reads the SAME EvidenceRecord back from the journal as a schema-valid evidence_pointer entry'; :85-91 'expect(journaled).toHaveLength(1);' / 'expect(entry.type).toBe("evidence_pointer");' / 'const reparsed = EvidenceRecordSchema.parse(entry.payload);' / 'expect(reparsed).toEqual(result?.evidence);'. `queryEntries({ type: "evidence_pointer" })` (:82) is the read side, `EvidenceRecordSchema` is 02's own schema, and `toEqual(result?.evidence)` pins the journaled payload to what `fireByTag` returned — so it is a round-trip, not two independent constructions.

The exhaustiveness half: :21 'const JOURNAL_ENTRY_TYPE_USAGE: Readonly<Record<JournalEntryType, boolean>>' — the `tsc -b`-enforced mechanism (a missing or stray key fails the build) — plus the two runtime guards, :49 'expect(Object.keys(JOURNAL_ENTRY_TYPE_USAGE).sort()).toEqual([...JOURNAL_ENTRY_TYPES].sort());' and :56 'expect(used.sort()).toEqual(["adjudication_decision", "evidence_pointer"].sort());'. The second is the one that bites: it pins the exact set of members this package writes, so adding a third would fail here.

Why 'EVERY emitted EvidenceRecord' is a structural claim and not a sample: :29 'const record: EvidenceRecord = EvidenceRecordSchema.parse({' and :51-56 'await journal.appendEntry({' / 'type: "evidence_pointer",' / 'payload: record,'. There is exactly one construction site and exactly one append, and the file-level comment at :16-20 states the invariant — 'gate firing by `./registry.ts`'s `fireByTag`/`fireAll` — individual gate' / 'modules never journal their own `EvidenceRecord` directly, so there is' / 'exactly one emission code path for every registrant'. `registry.ts:53-56`'s `fireOne` is the sole caller, so an EvidenceRecord that is not an `evidence_pointer` cannot be produced by a firing.

The one thing that could make the criterion read as false, checked and cleared. `ratchet-store.ts:138-144` — 'await journal.appendEntry({' / 'type: "adjudication_decision",' / 'payload: {' / 'decision: RATCHET_DECISION,' / 'rationale: JSON.stringify(observation),' — and `flake/quarantine-registry.ts` (next citation) do write a DIFFERENT member, which is exactly what interface-ledger Gap 5's Resolution (2026-08-01) records. But their payloads are `RatchetObservation`/quarantine entries, NOT `EvidenceRecord`s: the schema is `RatchetObservationSchema` at :44-51, four fields ('projectId: z.string().min(1),' / 'linePct: z.number().min(0).max(100),' / 'branchPct: z.number().min(0).max(100),' / 'observedAt: z.string(),'), none of them `objectId`/`command`/`exitStatus`. So the criterion's subject — emitted `EvidenceRecord`s — is untouched by that correction.

packages/gates/src/flake/quarantine-registry.ts:54-57 — 'await journal.appendEntry({' / 'type: "adjudication_decision",' / 'payload: { decision: QUARANTINE_DECISION, rationale: JSON.stringify(record) },'. The second of this phase's two `adjudication_decision` writers named in interface-ledger Gap 5's Resolution. Its payload is a quarantine entry (`testIdentifier`/`reason`/`expiresAt`), not an `EvidenceRecord`, so criterion 7's subject is unaffected.

The two OTHER EvidenceRecord writers in this package, checked so 'every' is not just 'every one the conformance test fires'. `tdd-gate.ts:74-76` — 'await journal.appendEntry({' / 'type: "evidence_pointer",' / 'changeSetId: input.changeSetId,' (`captureRedBaseline`, a pre-dispatch capture) — and `remote-evidence-pointer.ts:132-134` (phase 21, same three lines) both journal EvidenceRecords, and both use `evidence_pointer`. A repo-wide grep of `appendEntry` under `packages/gates/src` returns exactly five non-test sites: these two, `evidence.ts`, `ratchet-store.ts` and `quarantine-registry.ts`.
'Test Files  8 passed (8)' / '      Tests  38 passed (38)' — supplementary scoped local re-run at `eabb65a`, whose verbose output names all three conformance.test.ts cases individually.

criteria.notes: This is the phase the interface ledger's Gap 5 Resolution (2026-08-01) leans on, so the relationship is worth stating exactly. The ledger's 'Verified in' bullet still lists phase 14 against `evidence_pointer` alone; its own Resolution paragraph corrects that — '`coverage/ratchet-store.ts` and `flake/quarantine-registry.ts` write real `adjudication_decision` entries, carrying a discriminator in `payload.decision` and the structured record JSON-encoded in `payload.rationale`' — and `roadmap/14:88` already carries the matching dated annotation ('Mirror citation corrected 2026-08-01'). Both statements are true simultaneously because they are about different objects: this criterion is about `EvidenceRecord`s, which are all `evidence_pointer`; the ratchet and quarantine records are not `EvidenceRecord`s. criteria.notes: Fixture-modeled, and the criterion is worded for that: it says a green `engine-live` RECORD, and `journalFixtureGreenEngineLiveRecord` (:35-55) appends that record directly. No `@live` suite runs here and none was run for this closeout — `packages/gates` never imports `@crabgic/engine-claude`. The gate is a binding gate by design (roadmap/14 §Risks, 'Engine conformance stays version-grain by design'), so the absence of a live run is the specified behaviour, not a gap. Consistent with that, the four-way match at `engine-conformance-gate.ts:50-55` is what the record's authenticity rests on, plus the journal's own hash chain; a forged `evidence_pointer` entry with the right command string and fingerprint would satisfy the gate, which is a property of the journal's trust model (see `docs/threat-model.md`) rather than of this criterion.
